Linguistic analysis - part C

author: Heliana Teixeira date: 28-07-2021 code adapted from book “Text Mining with R: A Tidy Approach” at https://www.tidytextmining.com/tidytext.html

Using BBNJ dataset, Considering key Messages by Categories (#6) within SWOT levels (#4), through time (Negotiation.phase #3) This script applies keyword extraction techniques to analyse plain text and perform sentiment analysis. Clear R workspace

rm(list = ls())

2. Sentiment analysis

There are variety of methods and dictionaries for evaluating the opinion or emotion in text. binary positive and negative categories

get_sentiments("bing")
## # A tibble: 6,786 x 2
##    word        sentiment
##    <chr>       <chr>    
##  1 2-faces     negative 
##  2 abnormal    negative 
##  3 abolish     negative 
##  4 abominable  negative 
##  5 abominably  negative 
##  6 abominate   negative 
##  7 abomination negative 
##  8 abort       negative 
##  9 aborted     negative 
## 10 aborts      negative 
## # … with 6,776 more rows

assigns words with a score that runs between -5 and 5, with negative scores indicating negative sentiment and positive scores indicating positive sentiment

#install.packages("textdata")
library(textdata)
get_sentiments("afinn")
## # A tibble: 2,477 x 2
##    word       value
##    <chr>      <dbl>
##  1 abandon       -2
##  2 abandoned     -2
##  3 abandons      -2
##  4 abducted      -2
##  5 abduction     -2
##  6 abductions    -2
##  7 abhor         -3
##  8 abhorred      -3
##  9 abhorrent     -3
## 10 abhors        -3
## # … with 2,467 more rows

categorizes words in a binary fashion (“yes”/“no”) into categories of positive, negative, anger, anticipation, disgust, fear, joy, sadness, surprise, and trust.

get_sentiments("nrc")
## # A tibble: 13,875 x 2
##    word        sentiment
##    <chr>       <chr>    
##  1 abacus      trust    
##  2 abandon     fear     
##  3 abandon     negative 
##  4 abandon     sadness  
##  5 abandoned   anger    
##  6 abandoned   fear     
##  7 abandoned   negative 
##  8 abandoned   sadness  
##  9 abandonment anger    
## 10 abandonment fear     
## # … with 13,865 more rows

https://saifmohammad.com/WebPages/NRC-Emotion-Lexicon.htm

library(stringr)
library(dplyr)

Sentiment through the SWOT levels

bing lexicon

SWOT.sentim <- data_1 %>%
  inner_join(get_sentiments("bing"), by = c("Message" = "word")) %>%
  count(SWOT, index= msg.number,sentiment) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = sentiment, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>% 
  mutate(sentiment = positive - negative)

library(ggplot2)
ggplot(SWOT.sentim, aes(index, sentiment, fill = SWOT)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~SWOT, ncol = 2, scales = "free_x")

afinn lexicon

SWOT.sentim2 <- data_1 %>%
  inner_join(get_sentiments("afinn"), by = c("Message" = "word")) %>%
  count(SWOT, index= msg.number, value) %>%
  mutate(sentiment = value)

ggplot(SWOT.sentim2, aes(index, sentiment, fill = SWOT)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~SWOT, ncol = 2, scales = "free_x")

positive vs negative

library(reshape2)
## 
## Attaching package: 'reshape2'
## The following object is masked from 'package:tidyr':
## 
##     smiths
library(wordcloud)
## Loading required package: RColorBrewer
data_1 %>%
  group_by(SWOT)%>%
  inner_join(get_sentiments("bing"),by = c("Message" = "word")) %>%
  count(Message, sentiment, sort = TRUE) %>%
  acast(Message ~ sentiment, value.var = "n", fill = 0) %>%
  comparison.cloud(colors = c("gray20", "gray80"),
                   max.words = 40)

Sentiment through the Categories

bing lexicon

Cats.sentim <- data_2 %>%
  inner_join(get_sentiments("bing"), by = c("Message" = "word")) %>%
  count(Category, index= msg.number,sentiment) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = sentiment, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>% 
  mutate(sentiment = positive - negative)

library(ggplot2)
ggplot(Cats.sentim, aes(index, sentiment, fill = Category)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~Category, ncol = 2, scales = "free_x")

afinn lexicon

  inner_join(get_sentiments("afinn"), by = c("Message" = "word")) %>%
  count(Category, index= msg.number, value) %>%
  mutate(sentiment = value)

ggplot(Cats.sentim2, aes(index, sentiment, fill = Category)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~Category, ncol = 2, scales = "free_x")

positive vs negative

Sentiment through the Negotiation phases

bing lexicon

time.sentim <- data_3 %>%
  inner_join(get_sentiments("bing"), by = c("Message" = "word")) %>%
  count(Negotiation.phase, index= msg.number,sentiment) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = sentiment, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>% 
  mutate(sentiment = positive - negative)

library(ggplot2)
ggplot(time.sentim, aes(index, sentiment, fill = Negotiation.phase)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~Negotiation.phase, ncol = 1, scales = "free_x")

afinn lexicon

time.sentim2 <- data_3 %>%
  inner_join(get_sentiments("afinn"), by = c("Message" = "word")) %>%
  count(Negotiation.phase, index= msg.number, value) %>%
  mutate(sentiment = value)

ggplot(time.sentim2, aes(index, sentiment, fill = Negotiation.phase)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~Negotiation.phase, ncol = 1, scales = "free_x")

positive vs negative
